svg.title: CH347F EVT (CH347F-EVT-R0): the headers
svg.text: Top view, USB-B down, as WCH's photo. Each pin: its silkscreen, its function, and for the I/O lines their pins() name (IOn: WCH's GPIOn).
same chip pin as another header
The jumpers: none picks a mode (the CH347F has none: 1a86:55de, everything at once)
JP1, on its bottom pair (3V3 to VIO): the I/O lines and the I2C pull-ups at 3.3 V. Never on its top pair: that shorts VIO to GND.
P8: the flash's chip select. On its bottom pair (as delivered): SCS0; on its top pair: SCS1.
P7: what JTAG pin 7 (KEY) carries. On its bottom pair (as delivered): GND; on its top pair: 3.3 V.
U4, 24C02 EEPROM, on the I2C: SDA, SCL to the P5 lines; A0, A1, A2 to GND: address 0x50; WP to GND: writable; VCC 3.3 V.
U3, W25Q16 flash, on the SPI: CLK SCK, DI MOSI, DO MISO; /CS to P8's middle pin (SCS0 or SCS1 by its jumper); /WP, /HOLD to 3.3 V.
• Reminder: as delivered the flash's /CS is on SCS0, so a device on P4's SCS0 shares it (give it an I/O line as CS, or move P8's jumper); 0x50 is the EEPROM's.
• I2C is on UART1's flow-control pins: SDA on RTS1, SCL on CTS1, switched to I2C by a USB command (WCH's driver, and atiic, send it on opening).
• With I2C on, UART1 runs without flow control. DTR1 is also SPI's SCS1 (dashed: the same chip pin as on P4 and P8).
• SDA and SCL are pulled up on the board, 2 kΩ to VIO (R3 on SDA, R1 on SCL): a module's own pull-ups add to them.
• IO0 is CTS0, IO1 RTS0, IO2 DTR0 (UART0's modem lines); IO3 TRST, IO4 TCK, IO5 TDO, IO6 TDI, IO7 TMS (JTAG): none shares the SPI or I2C.
• UART0 and UART1 are the two serial ports, ttyACM on Linux. 3V3 is the board's 3.3 V (U1, from USB): power 3.3 V parts from it.
Board: WCH's photo (CH347EVT_EN V1.5), its KiCad design (CH347F-R0, 50 x 55 mm: the chips' pins by its nets), CH347SCH. GPIOs: CH347DS1 V1.6. The I2C switch: WCH's Linux driver. atiic docs/ch347.md.
